Stage 5 · Grammar

Grammar

my · your · his · her · its · our · their
1This is ___ brother. (I)
2___ name is Tom. (he)
3She loves ___ husband. (she)
4We visit ___ grandmother. (we)
5They sold ___ house. (they)
Why

I → my · he → his · she → her · we → our · they → their.

1___ name is Aisha. (she)
2We love ___ grandparents. (we)
3The cat drinks ___ milk. (it)
4They visit ___ cousins. (they)
Why

she → her · we → our · it → its (no apostrophe!) · they → their.

1___ name is Aisha. (she)
2We love ___ grandparents. (we)
3The cat drinks ___ milk. (it)
4They visit ___ cousins. (they)
Why

she → her · we → our · it → its (no apostrophe!) · they → their.

In other words
“This is my sister.”
“Her husband is a teacher.”
“Their children are twins.”
“What's your name?”
Notice

Notice: what comes after my, her, their — a person / thing, or nothing?

SubjectPossessiveExample
Imymy sister
youyouryour name
hehishis wife
sheherher husband
ititsits name (no apostrophe)
weourour children
theytheirtheir son
In other words
Use my / your / his / her / its / our / their + a noun: “my sister”, “his car”.
his = a man's · her = a woman's · their = more than one person's.
its has no apostrophe — it's = “it is”, but its = belongs to it.
Notice

Notice: what comes after my, her, their? Tell your partner.

In other words
Use my / your / his / her / its / our / their + a noun: “my sister”.
his = a man's · her = a woman's · their = more than one person's.
Notice

Notice: what comes after my, her, their? Tell your teacher.

In other words
Use my / your / his / her / its / our / their + a noun: “my sister”.
his = a man's · her = a woman's · their = more than one person's.
Stage 6 · Poss s

Poss s

Say who something belongs to.
Track 1.7 — 's: possessive or is?Original coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 Zafar's wife · Zafar's a doctor. 2 Their daughter · They're happy. 3 I'm his son. · He's my father. 4 Is he your brother? · You're right. 5 She's our teacher. · Are you married?
1“Zafar's wife” — 's =
2“Zafar's a doctor.” — 's =
3“He's my father.” — 's =
4“my sister's car” — 's =
Why

Zafar's wife = belongs to. Zafar's a doctor = Zafar is. Before a noun that belongs → possessive; before a/an, adjective or job → “is”.

1the book of Tom →
2the house of my parents →
3the crown of the king →
4the room of the twins →
Why

One person → 's. Plural ending in -s → just ': my parents', the twins'.

1“Zafar's wife” — 's =
2“Zafar's a doctor.” — 's =
3“She's our teacher.” — 's =
Why

Before a noun that belongs → possessive. Before a/an or a job → “is”.

1the flat of my sister →
2the house of my parents →
3the room of the twins →
Why

One person → 's. Plural ending in -s → just '.

1“Zafar's wife” — 's =
2“Zafar's a doctor.” — 's =
3“She's our teacher.” — 's =
Why

Before a noun that belongs → possessive. Before a/an or a job → “is”.

1the flat of my sister →
2the house of my parents →
3the room of the twins →
Why

One person → 's. Plural ending in -s → just '.

In other words
“This is my sister's flat.” = the flat of my sister.
“My parents' house is big.” = the house of my parents.
Belongs to…RuleExample
one person+ 'smy sister's flat · the king's crown
plural ending in -s+ ' onlymy parents' house · the twins' room
careful!it's = it isits = belongs to it
In other words
Add 's to a person to show what belongs to them: Tom's book.
If the word already ends in -s (plural), add just an apostrophe: my parents' car.
Careful: 's can mean “is” OR “belongs to” — listen to the whole sentence!
Stage 7 · Practice

Practice

Part 1 — Each sentence has one mistake. Choose the correct sentence.

2❌ “Him name is Marat.”
3❌ “The dog eats it's dinner.”

Why

my sister's flat · His name · its dinner (no apostrophe) · children is already plural → children's.

2Her son ___ a doctor.

Stage 8 · Read

Read

Read about a very famous family.
1The text is about…
Why

It explains who is whose son, wife, brother, aunt in the royal family.

1Prince Philip was the Queen's husband.
2King Charles is the Queen's son.
3Catherine is Harry's wife.
4William and Catherine have three children.
5Meghan is George's aunt.
Why

Catherine is William's wife. Meghan — Harry's wife — is George's aunt.

1___ husband was Prince Philip. (the Queen)
2William is ___ older son. (Charles)
3Meghan is ___ aunt. (George)
Why

the Queen → Her. One person's → add 's: Charles's, George's.

1Who was the Queen's husband?
2Who is the king now?
3Who is William's wife?
4Where do Harry and Meghan live now?
Why

Philip — the Queen's husband · Charles III is king · Catherine — William's wife · Harry and Meghan live in America.

1George is ___ nephew. (Harry)
2___ three children are George, Charlotte and Louis. (William + Catherine)
Why

Harry's nephew · two people → Their children.

1Who was the Queen's husband?
2Who is the king now?
3Who is William's wife?
4Where do Harry and Meghan live now?
Why

Philip — the Queen's husband · Charles III is king · Catherine — William's wife · Harry and Meghan live in America.

1George is ___ nephew. (Harry)
2___ three children are George, Charlotte and Louis. (William + Catherine)
Why

Harry's nephew · two people → Their children.

Stage 10 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1This is my ___ phone. (sister)
2My mother's father is my ___.
3My uncle's ___ is my aunt. (his marriage partner)
Why

Owner + 's: Aidar's phone, my sister's room \u2014 the owner comes FIRST.

1This is Aidars phone.
2My brothers name is Marat.
3The car of my mother is red.
Why

Owner + 's: Aidar's phone, my sister's room \u2014 the owner comes FIRST.

1Rewrite with 's: the phone of my sister
2Rewrite with 's: the room of my brother
3Whose is this? Answer for Marat.
Why

Owner + 's: Aidar's phone, my sister's room \u2014 the owner comes FIRST.
